An utterly compelling watch, I was thoroughly engaged from start to finish.
Gupta allows for the possibility that Ameet has come to guide Queenie through this last chapter and accompany her to the next life.
A Tupperware of Ashes has crafted a formidable character, and one that will be remembered.
Pooja Ghai and Tanika Gupta make a fantastic creative team, and have once again come together to create a piece of work that is entertaining, informative, and affecting.

The subject matter is resolutely affecting, with the impact of Queenie’s deterioration both upsetting to witness and on occasions even frightening - a testament to Syal’s total embodiment of the character.
This is an arresting piece of work that would be deserving of a larger audience in the Lyttleton.
Nitin Sawhney’s superb music likewise deepens the drama’s emotional journey.
A Tupperware Of Ashes is exceptional on every front.

cn.t: Gupta's dementia drama earns mostly positive reviews for Meera Syal's towering performance and emotional potency, though some critics find it overly linear and question its King Lear framework. The play's cultural specificity and gallows humor resonate powerfully.
